Volume One of the Extensive Record of Master Xizhou.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Xishi at Fulong Chan Monastery,
compiled by Attendant Facheng.
On the eighth day of the first month in the ninth year of the Chunyou era, the Master entered the monastery.
The Mountain Gate. The Great Gate of Liberation. There is no place for entry or activity; the profound pivot is severed. Every step is a living path. (He strides forward abruptly and says:
"What harm is there in walking a few steps with one's own feet?
The Buddha Hall. Deshan was soft and stubborn; Yunmen was acting foolishly. They cannot be saved. "Gautama, Gautama! (He then inserts [the incense burner]).
Fragrant Clouds: I have, for no reason at all, entered the noisy basket of the Abbot’s quarters.
The Mind-essence of China and the True Eye of India—facing each other directly, seizing the opportunity, both right and wrong are swept away.
Not falling into thought, one penetrates the precipice. (He shouts: You fellows standing below the steps!
The Imperial Edict: "In the family of patch-robed monks, the nostrils usually reach up to the heavens. Why, then, have they been pierced by this? Have you not heard it said:
'The ultimate transformation is difficult to escape'?"
A Brief Account of the Rivers and Lakes. Pushing people off a cliff; injuring others with malicious words. The grievance is as deep as the tides of the sea; gnashing teeth and biting the gums.
(Mute) When spoken of, it is nothing but malice.
Dharma robes. Without having entered Mount Jizu, one has not yet trodden the path of Huangmei.
Though one’s evil karma may seem slight, one will go forth clad in fur for no reason at all—a source of laughter before those with clear eyes.
The seat of the emptiness of dharmas— manifestly accomplished, seen, reached through practice, and expressed in speech— the Lamp-King of Mount Sumeru leaves behind no small amount of disarray.
The words of the hunter; the mechanism for trapping the tiger; the skill for slaughtering the dragon. When the Great Function manifests, there is no room for minor trials.
Is there anyone who can exert themselves without regard for their own person? Come forth and meet me!
The Master asked: "Auspicious vapors coil upon the mountain ridges in the vast sky; the ancient Buddha emits light once more this day. The student replied:

"Sick eyes see flowers in the air. He pressed further: "The wild plum blossoms brilliantly, its coldness encasing jade; it draws forth a pure breeze that carries its hidden fragrance. "The student has come forward;
I request the Master to offer prayers for the Emperor. The Master replied: "Ten thousand pines before Mount Taibai—throughout the year’s coldest season, none can compare to them."

[The Master] said, “The mind of a sage. [The student] asked, “Regarding the opening of the hall to offer prayers for the Emperor as directed by our Teacher, how was the matter of the transmission of the robe through the six patriarchs?
He replied, “The thief has no fixed form; he drums and entices. [The student] asked, “Who was the First Patriarch? He replied, “He offended the taboo name of King Liang;
sighing and distressed, he crossed the river in the dark. [The student] asked, “Who was the Second Patriarch? He replied, “A white staff snapped in two.”
[The Master] said, “A single arm. The questioner asked, “What is the Third Patriarch? He replied, “His whole body is raw and red; one cannot bear to look at him.
The questioner asked, “What is the Fourth Patriarch? He replied, “An empty fist deceiving a small child. The questioner asked, “What is the Fifth Patriarch?
He replied, “If he were to come again, he would not be worth half a penny. The questioner asked, “What is the Sixth Patriarch? He replied—
[The Master] said, "Stonehead fell and broke the donkey’s back. The student asked, "The Sixth Patriarch has already received your instruction;
as for the ultimate vehicle of the ancestral school, what is it? He replied, "Drops drip from the eaves, clearly and steadily.

The student asked, "In the past, when the Venerable Ding went to visit Linji and asked, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Is there anything definitive about it? Linji replied, 'Too much!'"
[The Master] calmly set aside his weapons and armor. As [the monk] stepped forward, [the Master] descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Speak!
Speak! I wonder, is there an instruction or not? [The monk] replied, "A sharp sword cuts through empty space; the ten thousand phenomena resound with a *pō-pō*.
[The Master] said, "If you deliberate, is this understanding or not? [The monk] replied, "Closing one's eyes to eat a snail—what a bitter and sour ordeal! [The Master] said, "..."
A monk standing by asked, "Venerable Ding, why do you not prostrate? Was there an intention to reproach him? Ding replied, "Giving a ladder to a thief.
The monk pressed further, "Why did that other monk prostrate and immediately attain enlightenment? Ding replied, "Ten thousand miles to Yuzhou is not far.
The monk pressed again, "An authentic master! His natural brilliance still remains," and he then prostrated. Ding replied, "Thief!"
The bribe was not accepted. Holding the main axis:
the path above is slippery; standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, it is perilous. Even a spark from flint or a flash of lightning is still dull.

Deshan and Linji employed the "precipice mechanism," yet their construction failed to penetrate. Nanquan and Zhaozhou possessed the eye to pass through the barrier, yet they could not look [deeply enough].
To see is to grasp it thoroughly and perceive it clearly; even ten thousand *li* away in Yuzhou is not far. What more need be said of "mind itself is Buddha"?
That is merely drawing lines on the ground to create a prison. "Neither mind nor Buddha"—that is like marking the boat's position to seek a lost sword.
In the end, what is it? (He strikes the meditation seat with his whisk and says: Before sound, after words—a fresh arrow from Silla.
Baoshou was inaugurating the hall. Sansheng brought forward a monk, and Baoshou immediately struck him.

Sansheng said, "To act as a teacher for others in this manner not only blinds the eyes of this monk, it will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou. Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
[The Master] took up the case and said: "Baoshou was indeed right, yet he was pitifully small-minded. Had he waited for Sansheng to..."
"What do you say? He then struck him with his staff in a harmonious tone. This shows that the lineage is penetrating and the eye is agile.
Since he let him off at that time, what about this present one? (He then laid his staff across his lap and looked left and right, saying: "Who dares to give a small evening lecture?
Floating on the vast waters by the shore of Lake Xizi, one sees the willows drooping along the cold green embankment. Who would have known..."
The debt of karma is difficult to evade; with eyes wide open, one enters the cauldron of boiling water with imposing dignity. At this point, how can one possibly manage?
If you intend to roast yams until they are soft, disregarding the purple clay seal [of official rank], you will still not avoid falling into the footprints left by the ancients.

If you intend to lock the void and imprison dreams, blocking the roads and breaking the bridges, you fear you may sit within a thicket of entanglements. It is better, therefore, to simply accept things as they are.
A bit. I shall now descend to accord with the exigencies of the times. (He then takes up his staff and says: "Vertically, it exhausts the three periods of time. (Holding it horizontally, he says:
"Horizontally, it spans the ten directions. (Tapping it once, he says: "The blue-eyed, yellow-headed ones cannot comprehend it. (Leaning the staff against him, he says:
"When the wild plum's breeze has settled, its fragrance floats on in secret."
Again, it is related: Beneath Nanquan Mountain there was a hermitage keeper. A monk passing by said, "Nanquan has recently appeared in the world; why do you not go up the mountain to pay him homage?

The keeper replied, "It is not only when Nanquan appears in the world that I would not go to pay homage; even if the thousand Buddhas were to appear in the world, I still would not go to pay them homage.
When Nanquan heard of this, he ordered Zhaozhou to go and investigate him. Upon arriving, Zhaozhou immediately prostrated himself. The keeper did not—

[The Master] looked back, moving from east to west and from west to east; the host did not look back either. Zhou said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated," then he pulled down the curtain and departed.
Upon returning, he recounted this to Nanquan, who said, "I have always suspected this fellow.

The verse says: With servile faces and cringing knees, he scurries through the world; Ashamed to see him, one thinks of the Seven Li Beach and his sheepskin robe. Though Wen-shu was indeed the Son of Heaven...
The son is noble. View Ziling merely as an old friend.
Ascending the hall for the King of Qi: Mountain rain brews a spring chill; at dawn it drenches the plum blossoms heavy. They will take longer to bear fruit.
"Listen now as the fragrance drifts and stirs; the Master of Transformation has a purpose and awaits your return. May you forever serve as the 'cauldron and tripod' to season the soup.
But tell me, who is it that returns? (He then rises and bows, saying: "Ten thousand blessings to the King of Qi on this Lantern Festival!
We thank the new and old classes of monks for ascending the hall. While people everywhere compete to enjoy the lanterns, at Fulong Monastery there is not even one."

It is so. Though I am ashamed of my own emptiness and meagerness in hosting this banquet, the distinction between guest and host is blurred by the shared joy. The moon over the mountain passes aids in casting its radiance;
the wind at the valley mouth arranges the rhythm. With sleeves dancing in the spring breeze, we celebrate the peace of the age.
Unaware that we stand here after the time of Dīpaṃkara. (Clapping his hands, he says: "A fine brother!"
The seventeenth day of the first month: offering incense on the anniversary of Chan Master Baizhang’s passing. A single shout deafens for three days; all personal possessions are lost.
He dug a deep pit to trap others, yet could not avoid groundless slander. For a thousand ages, it has served as the foundation for calamity within the monastic community.
How many smile with hidden mirth? How many weep in sorrow?
On account of a certain matter, he ascended the hall and related the story of Zhaozhou visiting Touzi. On the way, he encountered Touzi descending the mountain carrying a pitcher.
Zhaozhou said, "I have long heard of Master Touzi; I never imagined you were merely an oil-seller. Touzi replied, "You know only the oil-seller."
Furthermore, one does not recognize Touzi. Zhaozhou asked, "What is Touzi? Touzi held up a flask and said, "Oil, oil. [The Master] comments:
Everyone says that the old man Touzi is always without a single drop of leakage; why then was he scrutinized by Zhaozhou?
Even if one were to forge it with adamantine steel, it would still be不免 (unable to avoid) having hands stuck and feet mended.
On the first day of the second month, he ascended the hall and said: "The third elder brother and the fifth younger brother whistle at the moon and sleep amidst the clouds;

they gaze at the mountains and play with the waters. Having grasped the mouth, they have lost the nose. Suddenly, a man from among the assembly came forward and said, "The Buddha-dharma and the patriarchs' intent are just this!
Fulong did not spare him; lowering his eyebrows, he stepped forward, made a deep inquiry with a bow, and said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice."
Sound. Even walls and screens have ears.

(Ye Sin-ju) To the former and current administrators: (Eung Heung-ho) Miraculously responding to the myriad capacities of beings, one has found the path upon the broad highway amidst the vast flow of worldly dust.
How does one discern the master? Once the master is discerned, one may advance or retreat as appropriate, unhindered whether departing or remaining.
One mounts the three-legged donkey of Yangqi sideways and boasts of walking alone throughout the south, north, east, and west.
The Buddha ascends the hall for his final nirvana at Kuśinagara, beneath the twin śāla trees. His mortal remains are difficult to overturn; his true body is fully exposed.
This summons Māra, who breaks into a wild dance of laughter. The descendants of later generations have mouths like pestles; when they suffer injustice, to whom can they appeal?
Mountain flowers drip with tears of crimson rain.
Ascending the hall: A spring day is bright; the burn scars upon the earth are green. Patches of brocade-like clouds, the mist of flowers dense and deep. (Holding up the whisk, he says:
The True Person of No Rank enters and exits through the gate of the face. (He gives a shout: Thief! Spirit-thief!
Ascending the hall: One does not stop at one; if one does not rest at two. To receive a horse from another, one returns an ox to them. Have you not seen Lin...?

Three times he was struck with the white staff; three blows from the ribs of Daoyu caused such agonizing pain. An enemy against whom one cannot dwell under the same sky—mountains stretch on and on, waters flow and flow.
Vengeance is bound upon the tips of the hundred grasses in the spring breeze. Patting his knee, he says: "Enough, enough!
To speak of it makes one’s face blush with shame."

Ascending the hall to pray for fine weather, [the Master said]: "The staff of a patch-robed monk holds one sheng and three he of rice. This year the spring rains have been many; a single full meal will likely be hard to obtain.
When the Immortal of Mount Juehai heard these words, his hair bristled in rage like a helmet being donned; he drove forth spirits and commanded ghosts.
Slaying the cloud-masters and sweeping away the misty greens. (With the whisk, he draws a circle.
Releasing the golden crow as it emerges from the sea-gate, let us listen to songs and dances celebrating a bountiful year; we seek only one who does not acknowledge his debt of gratitude.
Ascending the hall on the Qingming Festival: On the days of Han-shi and Qing-ming, families perform their ancestral rites. Ash from paper offerings clings to butterfly wings;

tears shed in grief stain the flower branches. In pursuit of kin, they contemplate the distance; they inscribe their resentment and harbor their sorrow. Regardless of wealth or status, all are subject to this.

Only those monastics of the forests and springs—without thought, without recollection, without desire, and without action—recline peacefully upon their round cushions and idly play with their slender staffs.
As the swallows naturally flourish, the spring remains silent; let me sing one long song: *Luo-luo-li*. (Clapping his knee, he says:
"If it were not for one who knows this, to whom could I speak?"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The fangs and claws of the ancestors differ in a thousand ways and ten thousand variations. They shorten the cranes and lengthen the ducks; they wound the tortoises while showing leniency toward the turtles.
(Holding up the staff, he said: "This staff does not enter this protective community. It is muddled and vague, lame and crippled;

it has eyes but is as if blind, and a tongue but is as if tied. (Leaning the staff against him, he said: "It rests quietly at the foot of a pine tree, sleeping soundly without ever waking. From this, the Buddha-dharma..."
The teachings are as rotten as mud. (Waving his hand, he says: I will not speak, I will not speak. Entering the hall:
In this mountain retreat, spring is deep, yet our livelihood grows poorer by the day. The peach blossoms are in full bloom, yet Lingyun is nowhere to be seen. Why is this?
The house lacks the *Bai Ze* diagram. Entering the hall:
With meager merit, I dwell upon the mountain; there is truly no leisure day. When busy, it is as if at ease; when relaxed, it is most urgent.
He drove away the gardeners and servants, weeded the vegetable plots, and swept the pine groves. Pointing at the overseer Yang Tuan, he dismantled the eastern fence and patched the western wall;
the affairs before his eyes were as chaotic as hemp fibers, and beneath his feet it was as black as lacquer.
Suddenly, a man came forth and said, "Elder, why are you so preoccupied? He simply replied, "Even if it were the Seventh Patriarch himself, there would still be no such thing."
News. Upon returning from entering the capital, he ascends the hall: Barefoot, one runs through the red dust; The whole body enters the wild weeds. How much spirit has been wasted!
It is not as good as dwelling in the mountains. A valley of idle clouds, a thousand peaks of singing birds— Sound and form are pure and true; Right and wrong do not exist.
Arrived. Truly pitiable, truly laughable. Cold Mountain Man: after ten years he still could not return; he has forgotten the path by which he came.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] took up his staff and said: "Vibrant and agile, firm and resilient—those with clear eyes cannot see through it.
It is only the cuckoo of the spring mountains who knows it, shedding blood as it cries through the clear day. (He throws down the staff and says: "Leaping and bounding in the wind!"
The Southern Quarter. (He shouts: "Coming to the hall ahead of donkeys and behind horses.

This is the upward-tending mechanism, the eye at the crown of the head, the bowl slipping from the hand, the leaking oil lamp. All the patriarchs of the past have already erred in their handling and presentation of it.
Today, on this Buddha-peak, I shall clearly analyze and judge it. Do you understand? At night one sleeps; at mealtime one eats.
Picking tea and bamboo shoots, he ascends the hall. Shaking the tea tree, he steals the bamboo shoots away. A tiger with its horns emerges from the forest; an iron snake lies across the road.
Its poisonous breath blazes like a mass of fire. If you can see the intimacy [of this] upon raising your eyebrows, the sacred trace is not where the monkeys cry.
Ascending the hall: Pine pollen wafts its fragrance; wheat whiskers play in yellow. Today, spring bids farewell; nowhere can one find its traces.
The swallow understands the principle of non-migration and speaks deeply of the true mark (*dharmatā*). Perching upon the carved beam, it addresses you all, seeing that you do not understand.
Carrying mud to repair old fortifications, they fly over Mo Family Pond.
On this occasion, he ascends the hall and cites the verse of the Fifth Patriarch: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain; With palms joined, I earnestly question the patriarch:
How many times has it been sold and then bought back again? Out of pity for the pines and bamboo that draw in the pure breeze. He then remarks: "To the east..."
Old Man Shan is utterly lacking in self-mastery; with such a tiny plot of land, buying and selling it—when will it ever end?
Fulong is not like this: the ancestral fields have no boundaries; the deeds are clear, so who would dare encroach?
The spring winds have stripped away all idle grasses and trees; the pine waves toss the moon, and the bamboo filters the gold.

Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: struck with the staff, he does not die; drenched in water, he does not die. With both hands he gesticulates mockingly, his entire body stained and defiled.
Even if one were as spiritually potent as the head physician from the Buddha’s burial mound, in the end, how could one ever wash him clean?

Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat. On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, everywhere the summer retreat is entered; boundaries are drawn to form prisons, and one is bound by layer upon layer of shackles.
Only here at Yangtang does the cloud on Stone Chime Peak soar of its own accord, free from the constraints of coming or staying.
Why is this? "Climbing Mount Dong, one sees Lu as small; climbing Mount Tai, one sees all under heaven as small. (Patting his knee) Who knows who among us is a fellow student?
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said: 'Studying ten spiritual friends is not as good as studying one head seat;
studying ten head seats is not as good as studying one fellow practitioner; studying ten fellow practitioners is not as good as studying oneself. I, Fulong, am not like that:
In the Great Peace, there is no need to adjust the idle spears and armor; under a single pillow of pine wind, one is drunk in the blackness."
Sweet. [The Master] ascends the hall: "Fat horses bustle about; lean horses bustle about. To heal the sores before one's eyes, one gouges out the flesh from the heart.
Morning is not enough, evening is not enough. Six times six remains thirty-six. Do you understand? When Yunmen saw Muzhou..."
Liangsui visited Magu. Magu ascended the hall and said:
"When the myriad activities have ceased, one dwells amidst the clouds; the gate is closed by green vines, and all day long there is leisure. At times one hears a single song of 'ming-yi';
riding backward on a yellow calf, one emerges from the pine pass. If you understand this as the Buddha-dharma, it is like wrapping fine brocade around a rough stone. If...
He creates a worldly convention, like an iron-wrapped lump of clay; alas, no one understands this meaning. (Striking the meditation bench, he says:
"In the wind, I strike the stone balustrade."
A Letter from Mount Jingshan, Offering Incense: The father was unkind; the son was malicious. Hot blood sprayed one another; agonizing fists struck each other.
An enemy not to be shared under the same sky—pushed into the Avīci Hell. This grievance, this resentment—with whom can they be discussed?
Even the sea moon and mountain clouds break their spirits.

Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: There is a medicine that is remarkably effective; it is not found in the *Elhou Fangshu* (Recipes from Behind the Elbow), nor is it included in the *Shennong Bencao* (Shennong’s Herbal Classic).
Sudhana did not recognize its true nature where he gathered it; Mañjuśrī could not find its subtlety in his application.

(He picks up the staff and says: “Buddha’s Mound is grasped by the hand. (He strikes the ground with it and says: “The root source of all ailments is completely swept away. Do you all feel this state of total liberation?”
"Is it cool and refreshing? (After a long pause, he says: "Since it is already cool and refreshing," (he throws down the whisk and says:
"Why need this to ascend the hall? Smoke clears and the bamboo trees resound with the cries of the *gū-è*; the moon is cold as the pine tips wail for the *zǐ-guī*.
Do not say that each single cry merely shatters one's dreams; before you have returned, you must remember the time of arriving home."
At Tiantai, the Elder Kuiyi visited together with Shaoye. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "A person comes from Tiantai, leaving me a single scroll of the *I Ching*.
It reports: 'The same people enter the wilds; first they wail, then they laugh; in the end there is good fortune. I am a rustic from the fields of Fulong who has never known how to read books.
Having washed myself thrice and perfumed myself thrice, I have played with it without finding joy. Why is this? Who will take away my wealthy, magnificent mansion?"
Exchanging it for the poverty of a thatched hut.
Ascending the hall: Three days of sun, five days of rain; formless great peace, fields full of grain.

This is not a matter for deliberation on the Dharma, nor is it the circulation of worldly conventions. Even those with blue eyes and yellow heads do not know this. (Holding up his staff, he says: Greetings.
The Wheel-Wrinkled Master holds the staff. (He sets down the staff and says: "Remember this well.
When Daojue ascended the hall, (he held the staff crosswise and said: "When Deshan’s command is enforced, it is difficult to distinguish between right and wrong.
(He gives a shout. When Linji employs his means, the true and the false cannot be distinguished. This minor elder of Fulong lacks the power to tread in the footsteps of the ancients.
Traces. Gathering here and there as best one can to represent the "Gate-Wind" (the essential teaching style). (He throws down the staff and says:
"The staff has been used to transform living dragons. Even so, it still invites the laughter of bystanders."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] held up his staff: "Level as a mirror's surface, yet as perilous as a precipice; it admits no deliberation, nor does it belong to contrivance.
(He strikes the floor with the staff and says: "Finding a living path amidst a flash of lightning; attending a village feast within the Great Compassion Monastery.
The three summer months blaze fiercely, and sweat flows like rain. At Fulong, he fans himself, yet even the hand that wields the fan lacks strength.
What leisure have I to raise the mallet or brandish the whisk to explain yellow paths and black ways to you all? Even so, there are many who misunderstand.

[The Master] thanked the Supervisor for collecting the offerings and ascended the hall. (Raising the whisk) From where does this single grain arise? Before Yin and Yang were yet distinguished, the sprout had already begun to bud.

The first sprouting is the opening of the flower; a single river clearing of snow is the ripening of the fruit. Ten thousand acres of clouds roll across the sky as one gathers the harvest and returns with the fragrance filling the bowl.
After the meal, drumming the belly, one walks while singing. But tell me, by whose grace and power does this come about? (Looking left and right, he says: "Heh!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "In the sixth month, one buys the pure breeze; its price in the human world is likely beyond measure. At Fulong, poverty was uprooted and turned into wealth;
everything has been gathered up to rid you all of your feverish afflictions. (Holding the whisk, he makes a gesture of fanning and says:
"How refreshing for me! How delightful for me!"

Ascending the hall, he manifested the great capacity and clarified the great function: "In the sixth month, the Yellow River freezes to its very bottom. A thousand sages do not carry it; one's own spirit is not valued.
Wearing horns and donning fur, one acts as a being of a different species. He patted his knee and said, "A lacquer bucket! A lacquer bucket!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Right, right! A thicket of brambles, a field of gold. Not right, not right!

*Erala* and *candana*, nectar and thorns. Neither right nor wrong, neither not right nor not wrong. The crane, vigorous, departs with its fledglings; the monkey, at ease, returns embracing its offspring."

Ascending the hall, he said: "I do not concern myself with existence, nor do I concern myself with non-existence. When it is time for food, I open my mouth; when it is time for sleep, I close my eyes. Now tell me, whose realm is this?
(After a long silence, he said: "Even I do not know.
(He ascended the hall, then drew a single stroke with his whisk and said: "Fuxi’s single stroke: the primal simplicity was shattered and the original purity departed. Bodhidharma’s nine years..."

Sentiments forgotten and righteousness severed. From now on, carrying mud and hauling stones, bearing planks and rolling balls—perverse teachings will be difficult to support, and they will gradually lead to total extinction.
Reaching this point, what can be done? (He lets out a shout. Fortunately, clarity is like a mirror; why need it be crooked as a hook?
The Attendant Xie and the Rector (Vinaya-master) came to visit; I also thank the Supervisor of Revenues for ascending the hall.

Amidst the sound of the small jade chime and the rattling of the wooden barrel hoops, there is a sudden burst—secret function moving in concealment, danger divided and perilously deployed. Yet, in the Buddha’s field, there are not so many such matters:
harvesting the grain when the time is right, cooking fragrant rice from cloud-seeds, leisurely singing the mountain-dweller’s song, and strolling along the pine-gate path. Nevertheless.
Examining this from the future, it is just Zhao’s grandmother selling vinegar.

Entering the hall, the mountain monk said: "Before I arrived at this place, on the banks of West Lake and in the shade of South Mountain, while lodging under a cloud-canopied eave, I dreamed before Stone Bell Peak that a crimson light pierced the heavens.
At that time, I joined you all in raising our hands and touching our foreheads in joy."
He praised it with words of acclaim. Once he had arrived there, he ate his fill of *bāhulaka* rice; with a pillow of pine wind, his breathing was like thunder.
He wished to seek the state of the dream from the previous day, but it was utterly unattainable. Why? Because thieves do not enter the home of one who is vigilant.
Ascending the hall: Subtle as it enters a mote of dust, vast as it encompasses all without exterior. Should you attempt to take this upon yourself, you will lose your money and incur punishment.
Small retreat *sāman* (small-scale inquiry): At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, whether going east or west, even a monk with clear eyes will run into a pillar.
It reaches the point where even the *lilu* (the cat) and the *baigu* (the white ox) cause the earth to tremble and emit light; the blue-eyed one with the yellow head finds no way to hide his form.
Although this is so, it still involves traversing a journey. You must know there is yet a phrase for "arriving home. As for the phrase for arriving home:
when meeting a person three thousand miles away, you have cited it incorrectly.
[The Master] cited the case of Nanquan while he was hoeing a field. A monk came to visit him, and Nanquan said, "Go to the hermitage and prepare some food for yourself;
send me one portion up the mountain. (To the left, a straw rope binds a ghost-child.

The monk went to the hermitage, finished his meal, smashed all the household utensils at once, and lay down to sleep with his legs outstretched upon Nanquan’s bed. (In the sixth month, the Yellow River [is overflowing].)
At the bottom, it is frozen. When Nanquan saw that the meal had passed and no food had arrived, he returned home. He saw a monk who had broken the household utensils and was sleeping under the bed;
Nanquan also went to sleep against the wall. (Ten thousand acres of glass contain the autumn moon;

how could a broken chopstick stir up the turbidity? That monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. (The ocean dries up and its bottom is finally seen; when a person dies, they do not know their own heart. Later, Nanquan...
It is said: "Thirty years ago, there was a clever practitioner; to this day, one does not know where he has ended up.
(Two rows of tears upon the coral pillow: half are for thinking of you, half are for resenting you. The Master [Zhaozhou] remarked:
"Old Man Nanquan had the strategy to quell chaos, but lacked the sword to quell chaos. This allowed this monk to act so impudently. At that time, when he saw the monk on his bed...
While asleep, he set fire to the hut and burned it down. Even if this monk had possessed the path of liberation and were fully alive, he could not avoid his skull striking the ground.

Upon ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat, he shed the blood of the Buddha’s body and broke the harmony of the Sangha; with the jaws of a donkey and the chin of a horse, he merely flaunted his skills and boasted of his abilities.

The head honey-fruit: when the spring sun shines warmly, it vies in its loveliness; though frost and snow assail it, they cannot reach it.
Seizing the moment to harvest the grain, one attains both truths. Picked up with a casual hand, everything is wondrous. Vague yet distinct, vast and perfectly round—just like Yangqi’s chestnut thorn:
it cannot be split open, yet it can be swallowed. One’s entire household property has been overturned. Do you all still...?
Do you understand? (After a long pause, he slaps the meditation seat and says:

There is no small amount of disorder; old friends have arrived at the hall. The fragrant cassia drifts through the courtyard; the cold crickets chirp in the shadows of the steps. Every sound is a refined melody.
Dots and clusters of gold are brought forth in full measure to entertain honored guests. Though the Buddha’s mound is poor, it is not truly poor.
Even so, can it be called sound? Can it be called form?
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "There is a thing that no one recognizes. Sometimes it is in the southeast; sometimes it dwells in the northwest.
When one steps upon it while wearing broken straw sandals, its value is worth a thousand pieces of gold. Yet when carried back on the tip of a broken staff, it is not worth a single coin.
Whether you recognize it or not—it is the winter melon of Wu, the radish of Zhenzhou."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The single moon travels through the void; at a thousand gates, people gaze upon it in celebration. How many have eyes to see their own radiance?
Master Mazu and his son exerted all their strength to polish it, yet they could not obtain even half of it. Do you wish to see the true moon? (He draws a circle with his whisk and says:
How does this compare to a broken lacquer bowl?
Ascending the hall, he said: "The true command is fully upheld; there is neither 'being' nor 'not being. A winnowing basket has lips; Lake Dongting has no lid.
If you deliberate upon this as something extraordinary, you will enter hell like an arrow shot. If you do not deliberate upon this as something extraordinary, you will enter hell like an arrow shot."
Vice-abbot Xie, Chief Seat of the Quarters, Construction Supervisor, and Storekeeper: Ascending the Hall, one must maintain the living enterprise of Dongshan;
to sell ginger requires a fire. To continue the radiance of the Buddha-sun, how could there be no seeds of fire?

Although the Buddha’s mound may shift beams for pillars and dismantle the east to patch the west, when all is gathered and brought together, who among them does not fulfill their duty? It is indeed admirable, yet as the Ancient Sage said: "Mowing..."
The sickle for the rice harvest moves as swiftly as the wind. Furthermore, how can this be determined? Wait until this mountain monk has reached a conclusion; then I shall tell everyone:

on the first day of the ninth month, I shall ascend the hall. The place is remote and the clouds are deep; the autumn is high and the surroundings are still. The hall and chambers are desolate, with not a face to be seen.
The Wall. Although it is upon the ground of purity, who would willingly leave it in such disorder?
Ascending the hall: Autumn leaves drift and fall; autumn insects cry out at night. Form is not form; sound is likewise not sound.

There is no need for the eyes to see; one is permitted only to listen with the mind. That Bodhidharma could not be understood for nine years—he hurriedly took his single sandal and asked for the way home.
Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth: Sweet chrysanthemums spread their yellow; dogwood spews its fragrance. Yuanming misunderstood; he was merely indulging in the appreciation of the Double Ninth.

"Picking chrysanthemums beneath the eastern fence, the Southern Mountain remains ever-present before my eyes. (Patting his knee, he says: "He just said that flower branches have their own lengths and shortnesses."
Haizhuang returns to the Hall. With weary feet, he seeks the hermitage at Haimen; with whom can he discuss the past deeds of Tianyi?
The crane’s shadow sinks into the cold waters of the vast sky; standing gaunt in the autumn wind, how many souls have been broken?

Ascending the hall, he struck the incense burner and said: "Not knowing shame, they rouse the smoke from the tower; opening the eye of the *jiaoming* mosquito, they roll the hundred-flower ball. The four sevens and two threes roll on and on;
do not think that ten thousand *li* away there is no Yalou."
Ascending the hall: Above the head, vast and boundless; beneath the feet, vast and boundless. One cannot lift it up; the earth is wide and the sky is expansive. Why is this?
Because the old monk’s administrative duties are many.
On the anniversary of the Patriarch Bodhidharma’s passing, incense is burned. A rat stole from India and fled to China; they divided the loot over the fire, yet their descendants lack eyesight.
Though they have died and confessed in various quarters, they remain silent. Today at Fulong, the matter is clearly adjudicated. On what basis is this done?
